title: Reinforcing or Balancing? Loops From Ephesus to the Staff Room
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Classify six illustrative causal loops, two from Paul's world and four from school change, as reinforcing or balancing by counting the minus signs around each one.

educational.topic: Systems Thinking: Reinforcing and Balancing Feedback Loops
learningObjectives: Differentiate reinforcing from balancing feedback loops by counting the minus signs around each of six causal loops, two from Paul's world and four from school change, classifying at least 5 of 6 correctly on the first attempt.

dependencies: loops-ephesus-to-staff-room-cld.json (CLD JSON schema, one file for all six loops)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Rule application: classify each causal loop by counting minus signs, one scored attempt plus a hinted retry, with the count revealed after each answer and a summary table at the end
keyQuestions: How many minus signs are there around the whole loop, and is that number even or odd?
Why can a harmful loop be reinforcing?
What in the Ephesus loop plays the role that resistance plays in a school rollout?
commonMisconceptions: Reinforcing means good and balancing means bad; loops 3 and 6 are harmful reinforcing loops.
Any loop with a minus sign is balancing; loops 3 and 6 each have two minus signs and are reinforcing.
The number of variables decides the type.
assessmentOpportunities: At least 5 of 6 loops classified correctly on the first attempt.
Identify a real 'more initiatives' loop in a school, classify it, and propose how to weaken it.
